result.label: Own-price elasticity, 330ml can
result.rationale: Smallest, most impulse-driven format; set near the elastic end of the brief's -0.8 to -2.5 CPG range.
result.reference: Context only, not a fitted value. A 2024 meta-analysis of U.S. food demand elasticities (Jeon, Hoang, Thompson and Abler) finds household scanner data tends to give more elastic own-price estimates (https://pure.psu.edu/en/publications/a-meta-analysis-of-us-food-demand-elasticities-to-detect-the-impa/). It does not cover soft drinks specifically, so the values here are illustrative. A Marketing Science Institute working paper (Bray, Sanders and Stamatopoulos) finds observational scanner price variation does not reproduce experimental elasticities (https://www.msi.org/working-paper/observational-price-variation-in-scanner-data-cannot-reproduce-experimental-price-elasticities/), so the value carries a range that drives the sensitivity bands.

recommendations: Implement the aggressive 500 ml price increase as the lead option, as it gives the highest weekly gross profit while remaining within the supported range.
Keep the small price increase with light promotion support as a close second choice, as it lifts profit versus today with a gentler move on shelf.
Use the moderate 500 ml price increase as a fallback if you need a simpler plan without promotion changes, since it still improves profit over baseline.
Do not cut the 500 ml price toward the Gabor-Granger revenue maximum, as this reduces weekly gross profit versus today.
answer.summary:
The model says the aggressive 500 ml price increase gives the highest weekly gross profit, with the small price up plus promotion and the moderate price up also improving profit versus today, while the Gabor-Granger revenue-max price cut and input-cost stress both reduce profit. 
- Baseline – current 500ml PET price: weekly gross profit ₹2,27,764, used as the reference point.
- Candidate – moderate 500ml PET price up (~+7%): weekly gross profit ₹2,29,907, slightly higher than baseline as extra price largely offsets lower volume and some shoppers trade into other Aurora packs.
- Likely loser – aggressive 500ml PET price up (envelope ceiling): weekly gross profit ₹2,31,165, the highest profit as the higher price and some trade into other Aurora packs more than offset volume loss.
- Trade-off – small 500ml PET price up with light promo support: weekly gross profit ₹2,30,644, ahead of baseline because the price up and promotion gains outweigh the softer volume.
- Gabor-Granger revenue-index maximum ₹42.75 pet_500ml: weekly gross profit ₹2,25,886, below baseline because the price cut reduces margin more than the volume and cross-pack gains help.
- Gabor-Granger highest accepted price ₹45.00 pet_500ml: weekly gross profit ₹2,27,764, matches today’s profit in this data cut.
- Downside input-cost stress: weekly gross profit ₹2,16,721, well below baseline because higher cost of goods drags profit at unchanged prices and volumes.
